question: What is an epidemiological reservoir in simple terms?

options.A: A temporary holding tank for treated hospital waste
options.B: The natural home where a germ normally lives and multiplies
options.C: A man-made chemical used to destroy harmful bacteria
options.D: The sterile medical equipment used during surgery

explanation: Think of a reservoir as the natural hangout spot where a pathogen lives, grows, and multiplies so it can stick around over time! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h1)

question: What is the main difference between a reservoir and a source of infection?

options.A: A reservoir is always a non-living object, while a source is always an animal
options.B: A reservoir only contains viruses, whereas a source only contains bacteria
options.C: A reservoir causes mild symptoms, but a source causes deadly disease outbreaks
options.D: A reservoir is where the germ naturally lives, while a source is where you catch it from

explanation: You've got this! The reservoir is the germ's long-term home base, while the source is the immediate spot or item that passes it to you. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h1)

question: Which type of reservoir includes people who carry an infection without showing any signs or symptoms?
explanation: Spot on! Asymptomatic human carriers walk around feeling totally fine while unknowingly passing germs along to others. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h2)

question: What makes environmental reservoirs different from human and animal reservoirs?

options.A: They only transmit viral infections through the air
options.B: They cannot be affected by physical disinfectants
options.C: They consist of non-living things like soil and water
options.D: They require a living host to survive for more than an hour

explanation: Easy peasy! Environmental reservoirs are non-living parts of nature, like soil and water, that naturally harbor germs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h2)

question: Where does the reservoir fit in the chain of infection?

options.A: It provides the home and starting point for the infectious germ
options.B: It acts as the final portal of entry into the new host
options.C: It functions as the chemical agent used to sterilize instruments
options.D: It serves as the physical method of airborne transmission

explanation: The reservoir is always link number one—it's the cozy starting home where the germ hangs out before starting its journey. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h3)

question: A nurse puts a patient with a severe cough in a private room. Which part of the chain of infection is the nurse mainly controlling?
explanation: By isolating the patient, you trap the human reservoir and block the germs from escaping into the ward air! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h3)

question: In Nigeria, which animal is the main reservoir for the Lassa fever virus?
explanation: Correct! The multimammate rat is the primary natural reservoir for Lassa fever, shedding the virus in its urine and droppings. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h4)

question: Why do open-air abattoirs and local farming practices increase the risk of zoonotic infections?

options.A: They bring humans into close contact with animal fluids, tissues, and waste
options.B: They attract insects that purify contaminated local water sources
options.C: They lower the temperature required for bacterial survival
options.D: They eliminate all natural predators of disease-carrying rodents

explanation: Working closely with animal tissues and fluids during farming or butchering makes it easy for animal germs to jump to humans. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h4)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in community health?

options.A: To punish communities that fail to maintain basic sanitation
options.B: To eliminate all vector insects using chemical sprays
options.C: To detect and monitor disease patterns and potential reservoirs early
options.D: To manufacture and distribute expensive pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Surveillance is like our radar system—it helps nurses spot disease trends and catch outbreaks before they blow up. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h5)

question: A community nurse notices many residents with severe watery diarrhea who all use the same stream. What is the best immediate step?

options.A: Advise residents to stop washing their hands after using the toilet
options.B: Report the cluster and investigate the water source as a potential reservoir
options.C: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics to every healthy person in town
options.D: Close down the local hospital to prevent airborne contamination

explanation: When people sharing a water source get sick together, checking that water supply is a classic nursing move to find the culprit! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h5)

question: Which action directly targets a human reservoir to stop an infection from spreading?

options.A: Boiling all municipal drinking water before distribution
options.B: Placing metal wire mesh over livestock feed storage
options.C: Spraying heavy insecticides around outdoor garbage dumps
options.D: Administering curative drug therapy to clear the pathogen

explanation: Giving medications clears the germs right out of the human body, turning off that human reservoir. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h6)

question: Why is keeping rodents away from food storage a great way to prevent certain viral diseases?

options.A: It prevents animal reservoirs from contaminating food supplies with waste
options.B: It purifies the soil surrounding agricultural farming plots
options.C: It eliminates human asymptomatic carriers in crowded cities
options.D: It stops humans from consuming raw meat from infected cattle

explanation: Keeping rats out of food means they can't drop their infectious urine and droppings onto the grains and food we eat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h6)

question: What is a community health nurse's key role in preventing reservoir-based illnesses?

options.A: Isolating all livestock in urban residential neighborhoods
options.B: Designing and building modern municipal water treatment plants
options.C: Writing national health policies for pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.D: Educating the public on hygiene, waste disposal, and safe food storage

explanation: You are a teacher at heart! Teaching families simple hygiene and food safety habits is one of our most powerful prevention tools. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h7)

question: Why do clinical nurses need to team up with environmental health officers?

options.A: To replace the need for community health education programs
options.B: To ensure that hospital beds are only filled with surgical patients
options.C: To effectively address both the infected patient and the environmental reservoir
options.D: To reduce the cost of purchasing pharmaceutical drugs for clinics

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Treating the sick patient in the ward isn't enough if we don't clean up the environmental source causing the sickness outside. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h7)
